title: AIP-C01 Hands-on Labs: AWS Services Reference

AIP-C01 Hands-on Labs: AWS Services Reference

Every AWS service in the series: what it's for, when to use it, when not to, and the exam wording that points to it.

AIP-C01 Hands-on Labs · Reference page. Up to date with all of Domain 1 (Skills 1.1.1 to 1.6.6): 52 services and features, plus 6 commonly confused services. New posts add their services here.

Exam questions rarely ask what a service does. They ask which one fits a scenario, and the wrong options are usually real services used in the wrong place. So for every AWS service and feature in this series, this page answers four questions: what it's for, when to use it, when not to, and which words in a question point to it.

How to use this page

  • While reading a post: look up any service you don't know yet.
  • Before the exam: read the “Not recommended when” column, and the commonly confused services at the end. That's where most distractors come from.
  • Want to search or copy it? The same tables are in the companion repo as text, with the skill where each service first appears: github.com/prasanth2006z/aip-c01-labs, file SERVICES.md.

Models and model access

How your application reaches a foundation model, and how that model is served.

Choosing, customizing and releasing models

How a model is picked, adapted to a domain and replaced safely.

Bedrock retrieval (RAG)

Getting the right passages from your content into the prompt.

Bedrock prompts, safety and agents

Controlling what the model is told, what it may say, and what it can do.

Application and integration

The services around the model that receive requests, hold configuration and run the steps.

Data and storage

Where documents, state and vectors live.

Data preparation and processing

How data is checked, converted and cleaned before a model sees it.

Governance, observability and audit

How workloads are standardized, reviewed and watched.

Commonly confused services

Real services that often appear as wrong options. Know what they do, and when they ARE the answer.

Pairs the exam likes to mix up

  • Knowledge Bases vs fine-tuning: fresh facts from your documents vs learned behaviour and style.
  • Cross-Region inference vs Provisioned Throughput: more capacity with no commitment vs guaranteed capacity you pay for by the hour.
  • Flows vs Step Functions vs Agents: a fixed GenAI pipeline vs a long or multi-service workflow vs steps the model decides itself.
  • Function calling vs MCP: your own model decides when to call a tool vs many AI clients share the same tool.
  • Hybrid search vs reranking: find exact terms such as codes and names vs put the right passage first.
  • Guardrails vs prompt instructions: rules enforced outside the model vs requests the model may not follow.
  • AppConfig vs Secrets Manager: settings you change and roll out (model IDs, flags) vs credentials you protect and rotate.
  • Glue Data Quality vs Data Wrangler: automated rules on every batch vs visual exploration of a new dataset.
  • Transcribe vs Textract vs Polly: audio to text vs scanned documents to text vs text to audio.
  • CloudTrail vs model invocation logging: who called or changed something vs what was sent to and returned by the model.
  • Well-Architected Tool vs AWS Config vs Trusted Advisor: design review against best practices vs resource setting compliance vs account-level checks.
